title: regional-fleet-fallback-orchestrator-and-residency-guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a regional/multi-zone fallback orchestrator and residency guardrails for Dedicated fleets. The goal is to provide throughput guarantees and predictable autoscaling while enforcing customer data residency constraints. This ticket covers the placement policy engine, failover prioritization, autoscaler metric composition, and operator controls for residency-sensitive tenants. Work must preserve SLOs (p95 latency & throughput SLAs) and provide clear observability and telemetry for post-mortem analysis.
activity: 2025-01-10 - Triage: Raised after PM-7041 call with enterprise customers requesting stronger residency guarantees for Dedicated. Assigned to Marc.

2025-01-14 - Architecture sync: Decided on a layered policy model: hard-residency (no cross-country), soft-residency (prefer local but allow fallback), and permissive. Action: prototype policy evaluator service.

2025-01-22 - Prototype complete: evaluator accepts fleet tags, request residency tag, and returns ranked candidate zones. Early perf shows 1.2ms median evaluation latency. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-22571+Policy+Prototype
2025-01-28 - Design review: PM/Platform/Compliance feedback captured. Compliance insists on explicit audit trail for cross-border fallbacks and opt-in for soft-residency. Added audit event spec.
2025-01-30 - Implementation started: added placement score that factors latency delta, capacity headroom, and residency penalty. Initial commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/placement/pull/87

2025-02-02 - Autoscaler changes: new composite metric implemented (tokens_per_sec weighted with queue_depth). Bench results: reduces overprovisioning by ~18% on mixed workloads. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/214
2025-02-03 - Security review requested: submitted ticket to security ops and attached audit event schema. Security requested additional KMS access control for residency flags in private deployments.

2025-02-04 - QA: Running canary on internal Dedicated cluster with two customers (internal dev teams). Monitoring for failover jitter and cache warming impact. Canary dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/eng/ENG-22571-canary
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator returns ranked placement decision within 5ms median latency for 99th percentile of requests.
Hard-residency tenants never route to an out-of-country zone and generate an audit event when rejected due to capacity.
Soft-residency tenants prefer same-country/region but will failover only to pre-approved fallback zones; all fallbacks emit audit events and customer-notification hooks.
Autoscaler scales throughput-bearing pools based on composite metric and maintains p95 latency within agreed SLA for dedicated reserved customers during 2x load spike tests.
Telemetry: per-request placement decision, residency tag, fallback reason, and post-failover latency are logged and visible in Console within 5 minutes.
E2E tests exercising residency policies and failover paths are added to CI and green in canary pipeline.
technical_approach: Introduce a placement-orchestrator microservice that evaluates placement policies in three stages: eligibility filtering (residency and model compatibility), scoring (latency headroom, capacity, cost, residency penalty), and decision enforcement (assign primary zone and warm standby). Autoscaler will incorporate a composite metric: tokens_per_second * latency_weight + queue_depth * queue_weight, with knobs per-customer. Failover behavior defaults to soft-fallback with warm-standby pools; hard-residency customers are assigned only to eligible zones and get capacity reservations. Audit events are emitted to the telemetry pipeline with residency_reason fields. For private/VPC deployments, placement flags are stored encrypted and validated locally to avoid exporting residency metadata to control plane.
risks: Cross-zone warm-standby increases GPU costs; mitigation: configurable cost cap and prioritization of burst pools over long-term duplication.
Cache warming on failover can increase latency spikes; mitigation: asynchronous prefix/KV cache pre-warm and progressive request steering to let cache build without violating SLOs.
Incorrect policy configuration could block traffic for high-residency customers; mitigation: safe default to allow manual override and emergency bypass with audit logging.
Telemetry volume increase from per-request placement logs; mitigation: sampling strategy and aggregated retention in Console.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal dogfood): deploy orchestrator to internal Dedicated fleet, enable for internal-dev tenants only. Observe metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (select customers): enable soft-residency for small set of enterprise customers behind feature flag; require signed opt-in and notify SRE on enablement.
Phase 3 (wider rollout): enable hard-residency support for customers with reserved capacity; provide UI controls in Console for residency policy selection.
Phase 4: full default enforcement for new Dedicated customers; migration tooling for existing customers to declare residency preferences.
